I see what's happening. The code has already been implemented (this is the worktree with the changes). Let me understand the test failures better.

The cycle orchestrator now reads `current_iter` unconditionally - but the comment says "A fresh cycle has current_iter=0 (set by _cycle_state_init via //=), so _start_iter defaults to 1 — identical behaviour to the old hard-coded 1."

The finding says this breaks:
- `cycle-inner-iter-resets-per-outer-iter-test.sh`
- `nested-loop-rounds-test.sh`
The next lines name two more failing tests, nested-loop-rounds-build-test.sh and cycle-member-dispatch-events-test.sh. I'm reasoning that the orchestrator reads a stale current_iter left over from an earlier inner-cycle run, and that because _cycle_state_init uses //=, the value isn't reset to 0 on the next run, so the inner cycle starts at the wrong iteration.

Because `//=` only assigns when the key is absent, a previous run's `current_iter` never gets reset. So on the second pass of an outer loop, the inner cycle would resume from the stale value rather than starting fresh at zero.

I'm noting that the design's proposed fix would need to be more precise: persisted `current_iter` should only be used as the loop start when `resume_mode` is set, and fresh runs or new outer-loop iterations should always start at 1. I still need to work out how the orchestrator can tell whether it is resuming.

I'm checking whether the orchestrator actually receives a resume_mode flag, since the fix depends on being able to tell a resumed run from a fresh one.

_cycle_orchestrator_run_body() {
    local cycle_id="$1" state_dir="$2" state_file="$3"
    # Capture caller's errexit FIRST — orchestrator runs with set +e internally
    # so a stage failure doesn't yank the rug out from a set-e-active caller.
    # Restored before every return path via the { ...; return N; } idiom.
    local _ORCH_HAD_E=0; case $- in *e*) _ORCH_HAD_E=1 ;; esac
    set +e
    if [[ -z "$cycle_id" || -z "$state_dir" || -z "$state_file" ]]; then
        error "cycle_orchestrator_run: cycle_id, state_dir, state_file required"
        _CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON="config_invalid"; _CYCLE_LAST_OUTCOME="interrupted"
        { [[ $_ORCH_HAD_E -eq 1 ]] && set -e; return 1; }
    fi

    # ADR-029 G2/G3 cross-iteration persistence (#844): capture the outer cycle's

    local _parent_cid="${_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID:-}"
    _CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="$cycle_id"
    _CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=0
    _CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON=""

    # #833: reset per-iter cycle-banner seq counters for this run.
    _CYCLE_IO_SEQ=()

set -euo pipefail

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh

# shellcheck source=../../core/state/artifact-persist.sh

print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-3] --from-stage rehydrates prior-stage artifacts and skips their stage.start"

S3_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"
S3_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-state"
S3_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-events"
S3_EVENTS_JSONL="$S3_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
S3_STATE_FILE="$S3_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
mkdir -p "$S3_STATE_DIR/artifacts" "$S3_EVENTS_DIR"

# Create a git repo; _artifact_persist_snapshot writes the state branch here.
S3_WORK_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo fs-rehydrate-s3)"

  cd "$S3_WORK_REPO" && _artifact_persist_snapshot "$S3_STATE_DIR" "$S3_ID" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-snap.log" 2>&1 || _s3_snap_rc=$?

# ── Resume / fresh-start policy ────────────────────────────────────────────
    if $resume_mode; then
        # Explicit --resume: check state exists and honour --force for aborted
        if [[ ! -f "$state_file" ]]; then
            error "No state file found at $state_file; cannot resume"
            return 1
        fi
        local existing_status
        existing_status="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.status' '')"
        if [[ "$existing_status" == "aborted" ]] && ! $force; then
            error "Pipeline status is 'aborted'; use --force to resume anyway"
            return 1
        fi
        if [[ "$existing_status" == "complete" ]]; then
            warn "Pipeline status is 'complete'; starting fresh"
            resume_mode=false
        else
            # Restore run_id and issue from existing state
            _runner_run_id="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.run_id' "$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)-$$")"
            _runner_issue="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.issue' '0')"
        fi

        # Auto-resume policy
        local recommendation
        recommendation="$(get_resume_recommendation "$state_file")"
        case "$recommendation" in
            auto_resume)

# ─── _runner_resume_rehydrate <issue> <state_dir> (#1805, ADR-006 §3.6) ─────
# Restore completed-stage artifacts from the git state branch into the
# artifact area before the dispatch loop runs. Non-fatal on restore failure;
# a still-absent artifact is caught by the dispatch loop's stale-artifact
# check which now exits 1 instead of warning-and-continuing (SPEC-2 / SPEC-9).
_runner_resume_rehydrate() {
    local _rr_issue="$1" _rr_state_dir="$2"
    local _rr_artifacts_dir="$_rr_state_dir/artifacts"
    local _rr_staging="$_rr_state_dir/resume-rehydrate.staging"
    rm -rf "$_rr_staging" 2>/dev/null || true
    _artifact_persist_restore "$_rr_issue" "$_rr_staging" || {
        rm -rf "${_rr_staging:?}" 2>/dev/null || true
        return 0
    }
    if [[ -d "$_rr_staging/artifacts" ]]; then
        _artifact_persist_put_back "$_rr_staging/artifacts" "$_rr_artifacts_dir" || true
    fi
    rm -rf "${_rr_staging:?}" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_from_stage_preflight <stages_arr> <from_stage> <state_dir> <plugins_root> ─
# For --from-stage <s>: restore + put_back artifacts from the git state branch,
# then verify every stage before <s> has its primary artifact in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR.
# Exits 1 naming the missing stage in stderr. (SPEC-3, SPEC-4, ADR-006 §3.6)
_runner_from_stage_preflight() {
    local -n _fsp_stages="$1"
    local _fsp_from_stage="$2" _fsp_state_dir="$3" _fsp_plugins_root="$4"
    local _fsp_artifacts_dir="$_fsp_state_dir/artifacts"
    local _fsp_staging="$_fsp_state_dir/from-stage-preflight.staging"

    # Restore + put_back (same sequence as _runner_resume_rehydrate)

    if [[ -d "$_fsp_staging/artifacts" ]]; then
        _artifact_persist_put_back "$_fsp_staging/artifacts" "$_fsp_artifacts_dir" || true
    fi
    rm -rf "${_fsp_staging:?}" 2>/dev/null || true
    # Verify every stage before the target has its primary artifact
    local _fsp_s _fsp_plugin_dir _fsp_manifest _fsp_prim_path _fsp_resolved

        [[ "$_fsp_s" == "$_fsp_from_stage" ]] && break
        _fsp_plugin_dir=""; _fsp_manifest=""; _fsp_prim_path=""; _fsp_resolved=""
        _fsp_plugin_dir="$(_find_plugin_for_stage "$_fsp_s" "$_fsp_plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"

# ─── _artifact_persist_restore <issue> <restored_dir> [repo_root] ───────────
# Extract the tip of the state branch into <restored_dir> (created if absent).
# Prefers a local refs/heads/<branch>; falls back to refs/remotes/origin/<branch>
# when only the fetched remote ref is present (CI). No-op (rc 0, empty dir) when
# no state branch exists. Never touches the working tree.
_artifact_persist_restore() {
    _artifact_persist_reset_status
    local issue="${1:-0}" restored_dir="$2" repo_root="${3:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}"
    # Resolve the SHARED git dir (see _artifact_persist_git_dir). Two reasons:
    #   1. refs must be read from the shared store, not a per-worktree view;
    #   2. the old guard tested `-d "$repo_root/.git"`, which is FALSE in a linked
    #      worktree because .git is a file there — restore would silently no-op and
    #      prior artifacts would never come back, with no error to notice.
    local _gd=""
    [[ -n "$repo_root" ]] && _artifact_persist_git_dir_v _gd "$repo_root"
    [[ -z "$restored_dir" ]] && { _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no restored_dir given"; return 2; }
    if [[ -z "$repo_root" || ! -d "$_gd" ]]; then
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="unresolvable repo: repo_root=[${repo_root:-<empty>}] git_dir=[${_gd:-<empty>}] cwd=[$PWD]"
        return 1
    fi

    local branch; _artifact_persist_branch_v branch "$issue"
    local ref=""
    if GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/heads/$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ref="refs/heads/$branch"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SOURCE="local"
    elif GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/remotes/origin/$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ref="refs/remotes/origin/$branch"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SOURCE="remote"
    else
        # A first-ever run for this issue. Genuinely nothing to restore — the one
        # early return here that is NOT a failure.
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no $branch locally or on origin (first run)"
        return 0
    fi

        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="mkdir -p $restored_dir failed"
        return 1

    # #1878: PIPESTATUS, not the pipeline rc — a failing `git archive` piped into
    # a happy `tar` yields rc=0, so a broken restore reported success.

        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="restore of $ref failed (archive rc=${_st[0]} tar rc=${_st[1]}): ${err:-<no stderr>}"

    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="restored from $ref"

    # When env=0 AND template has cycles, emit `cycle.disabled reason=env_override`
    # PLUS a stderr banner BEFORE the linear path runs (silent-failure #3).
    local _template_has_cycle=0 _u
    if [[ ${#_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        for _u in "${_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS[@]}"; do

    local id="$1" kind="${2:-agent}" exit_code="${3:-0}" platform="${4:-}" role="${5:-}" version="${6:-0.0.1}"

    local fn; fn="${id//-/_}_run"

id: $id

EOF
    [[ -n "$platform" ]] && printf 'platform: %s\n' "$platform" >> "$dir/manifest.yaml"

EOF

${fn}() {

# Usage: zb_engine_loop_state <state_file> <loop id> <rounds> <limit> <final status>
zb_engine_loop_state() {
    local sf="$1" id="$2" rounds="$3" limit="$4" final="$5" root
    root="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)"
    ( source "$root/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1
      _cycle_state_init "$sf" "$id" "$(dirname "$sf")/$id-history.jsonl" "$limit" || exit 1

}

    local _vpp
    _verdict_primary_output_path_v _vpp "${1-}"
    [[ -n "$_vpp" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$_vpp"

# _verdict_primary_output_path_v <var> <manifest> — the same, read by the shell

_verdict_primary_output_path_v() {
    local -n _vpo="$1"; _vpo=""
    local manifest="${2-}" l v in_out=0 cpath="" cprim=""
    [[ -f "$manifest" && -r "$manifest" ]] || return 0
    declare -F _mg_clean_v >/dev/null 2>&1 \
        || source "$_ZBUILD_VERDICT_ROOT/scripts/lib/manifest-graph.sh"
    local re_open='^outputs:' re_top='^[a-zA-Z_]' re_id='^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*id:'
    local re_kv='^[[:space:]]+(path|primary):'
    while IFS= read -r l || [[ -n "$l" ]]; do
        [[ "$l" =~ $re_open ]] && { in_out=1; continue; }
        [[ "$l" =~ $re_top ]] && in_out=0
        (( in_out )) || continue
        if [[ "$l" =~ $re_id ]]; then
            [[ "$cprim" == "true" && -n "$cpath" ]] && { _vpo="$cpath"; return 0; }

            v="${l#*:}"; _mg_strip_lead_v v; _mg_clean_v v
            if [[ "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" == path ]]; then cpath="$v"; else cprim="$v"; fi
        fi

    [[ "$cprim" == "true" && -n "$cpath" ]] && _vpo="$cpath"
    return 0

_artifact_persist_snapshot() {
    _artifact_persist_reset_status
    local state_dir="$1" issue="${2:-0}" repo_root="${3:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}"
    # #1921: "amend" replaces the branch tip instead of committing on top of it.
    # persist must snapshot twice — the first snapshot cannot contain the result
    # file that describes it — and a second commit whose only delta is a status
    # file is the commit spam ADR-050 §4 rules out. Callers pass this ONLY when
    # they created the current tip themselves this invocation; amending a tip
    # written by someone else would discard a legitimate boundary snapshot.
    local mode="${4:-}"
    # Resolve the SHARED git dir before the guard uses it. The guard previously
    # tested `-d "$repo_root/.git"`, which is FALSE in a linked worktree (.git is
    # a file there), so persistence would silently no-op inside a worktree.
    local _gd=""
    [[ -n "$repo_root" ]] && _artifact_persist_git_dir_v _gd "$repo_root"
    # #1878: this is NOT "nothing to do" — it means we could not resolve a repo to
    # persist INTO, which is a real failure the caller must be able to see. It
    # used to `return 0`, which the runner reported as a successful snapshot.
    if [[ -z "$repo_root" || ! -d "$_gd" ]]; then
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="unresolvable repo: repo_root=[${repo_root:-<empty>}] git_dir=[${_gd:-<empty>}] cwd=[$PWD]"
        return 1
    fi
    local art_dir="$state_dir/artifacts"
    if [[ ! -d "$art_dir" ]]; then
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no artifact dir at $art_dir"
        return 0
    fi

    local branch; _artifact_persist_branch_v branch "$issue"
    # A NON-existent path: git initializes a fresh index there. A pre-created
    # empty file (plain mktemp) is rejected as "index file smaller than expected".
    local tmp_index
    if ! _artifact_persist_tmp_name_v tmp_index zbuild-persist-idx; then
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no free name for the throwaway index (TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/tmp})"
        return 1
    fi

    # Build a tree from the artifact files under a stable prefix (artifacts/…),
    # plus a couple of top-level state docs, in a throwaway index.
    #
    # #1878: SKIP a file we cannot stage, do not abort the snapshot. This loop
    # used to `break` on the first failure, discarding every artifact already
    # staged — while the `extra` loop below has always skipped-and-continued. A
    # file that vanished mid-scan (the artifact area has live writers) or is
    # unreadable must cost us that one file, not the whole snapshot.
    local added=0 skipped=0 f rel blob first_skip="" n

setup_git_temp_repo() {
    local name="${1:-gitrepo}"
    local repo="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name"
    mkdir -p "$repo" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    (
        # #2103 / ADR-024: the cd MUST be fatal. `set -e` is inert inside this
        # subshell because its status is tested by `|| return 1` below, so a
        # failed cd would otherwise run every git command in the CALLER'S
        # checkout — which is exactly what committed seed.txt into a real
        # worktree and pushed a branch to the real origin on 2026-09-15.
        cd "$repo" || exit 1
        # Use the real git binary (not whatever PATH shim may be present).
        local real_git
        real_git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || true)"
        # If a shim like the parity-fixture mock is on PATH, fall back to
        # well-known absolute locations.
        if [[ -z "$real_git" ]]; then
            for c in /usr/bin/git /usr/local/bin/git /opt/homebrew/bin/git; do
                [[ -x "$c" ]] && real_git="$c" && break
            done
        fi
        [[ -z "$real_git" ]] && return 1
        "$real_git" init -q -b main 2>/dev/null || "$real_git" init -q
        "$real_git" config user.email "test@zbuild.local"
        "$real_git" config user.name "zbuild-test"
        "$real_git" config commit.gpgsign false
        echo "seed" > seed.txt
        "$real_git" add seed.txt
        "$real_git" commit -q -m "seed"
        # Normalize default branch name to 'main' for predictable tests.
        local cur
        cur="$("$real_git" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
        if [[ "$cur" != "main" ]]; then
            "$real_git" branch -m "$cur" main 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$repo"
}

# ── setup_git_master_origin (#2103) ──────────────────────────────────────────

zbuild_engine_tmpdir_v() {
    local -n _etdo="$1"
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH:-}" && -d "${ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH}" && -w "${ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH}" ]]; then
        _etdo="$ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH"; return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}" && -d "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}" ]]; then
        if [[ -d "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/runtime" ]] || mkdir -p "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/runtime" 2>/dev/null; then
            _etdo="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/runtime"; return 0
        fi
    fi
    # #2017: the last resort is the DATA ROOT, not ${TMPDIR}. ADR-059 §1 makes
    # the path the keying — a reclaimer deletes a `runs/<id>/` or an
    # `issues/<N>/` and the scope follows from where it sits — so a ${TMPDIR}
    # answer is unreclaimable by construction. ${TMPDIR} survives only if the
    # data root cannot be created, because failing a run over a temp file is
    # worse than a stray directory.
    local _dr="${ZBUILD_DATA_ROOT:-${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT:-$HOME/.zbuild}}/tmp"
    if mkdir -p "$_dr" 2>/dev/null; then
        _etdo="$_dr"; return 0
    fi
    _etdo="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
}

atomic_write() {
    # --bak keeps the previous content in <target>.bak: only state recovery
    # (core/state: read_state, locked_state_update; resume) reads one back, so
    # only the state writers ask for it (ADR-065 §5, round 4).
    local bak=0
    if [[ "${1:-}" == "--bak" ]]; then bak=1; shift; fi
    local target="$1"

# file that vanished mid-scan (the artifact area has live writers) or is
    # unreadable must cost us that one file, not the whole snapshot.
    local added=0 skipped=0 f rel blob first_skip="" n
    local -a _abs=() _rel=()
    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        _abs+=("$f"); _rel+=("artifacts/${f#"$art_dir"/}")
    done < <(find "$art_dir" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
    # Include a handful of top-level state docs when present (scope manifest etc.).
    local extra
    for extra in scope-manifest.md intake.md; do
        [[ -f "$state_dir/$extra" ]] || continue
        _abs+=("$state_dir/$extra"); _rel+=("$extra")
    done

    # #2249: two git calls for the whole set — `hash-object --stdin-paths` and
    # `update-index --index-info` — instead of two per file (a run snapshots
    # after every stage, over hundreds of files). Any failure in the batch (an
    # unreadable file aborts hash-object) falls back to the per-file loop below,
    # so #1878's rule holds: a file we cannot stage costs only that file.
    if _artifact_persist_stage_batch "$_gd" "$tmp_index"; then
        added=${#_abs[@]}
    else
        rm -f "$tmp_index"
        for (( n = 0; n < ${#_abs[@]}; n++ )); do
            f="${_abs[$n]}"; rel="${_rel[$n]}"
            if ! blob="$(GIT_DIR="$_gd" git hash-object -w "$f" 2>/dev/null)"; then
                skipped=$((skipped + 1)); [[ -z "$first_skip" ]] && first_skip="$rel (hash-object)"
                continue
            fi
            # #1878: a refused entry is a skip, never counted as staged.
            if ! GIT_INDEX_FILE="$tmp_index" GIT_DIR="$_gd" \
                    git update-index --add --cacheinfo "100644,$blob,$rel" 2>/dev/null; then
                skipped=$((skipped + 1)); [[ -z "$first_skip" ]] && first_skip="$rel (update-index)"
                continue
            fi
            added=$((added + 1))
        done
    fi

    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED="$skipped"

    # Nothing staged at all. If files were SKIPPED that is a failure (we had work
    # and lost it); if there were simply no files, it is an honest empty.
    if [[ "$added" -eq 0 ]]; then
        rm -f "$tmp_index"
        if [[ "$skipped" -gt 0 ]]; then
            _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
            _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="all $skipped file(s) unstageable, first: $first_skip"
            return 1
        fi

# ─── _artifact_persist_stage_batch <git_dir> <index> (#2249) ─────────────────
# Stage _abs[] (paths) / _rel[] (names in the tree) into <index> in two git
# calls. The two arrays are NOT parameters: they are the caller's locals, read
# through bash dynamic scope, so only _artifact_persist_snapshot (which fills
# them) may call this. A tab inside a path is safe: --index-info takes the path
# as everything after the first tab (artifact-persist-batch-test B4).
# rc 1 — nothing trusted — when either call fails, a path holds a newline
# (stdin is line-delimited), or the blob count does not match.
_artifact_persist_stage_batch() {
    local gd="$1" idx="$2" paths="" blobs info="" i b
    (( ${#_abs[@]} > 0 )) || return 1
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#_abs[@]}; i++ )); do
        [[ "${_abs[$i]}" == *$'\n'* || "${_rel[$i]}" == *$'\n'* ]] && return 1
        paths+="${_abs[$i]}"$'\n'
    done
    blobs="$(GIT_DIR="$gd" git hash-object -w --stdin-paths 2>/dev/null <<< "${paths%$'\n'}")" || return 1
    local -a _b=()
    mapfile -t _b <<< "$blobs"
    (( ${#_b[@]} == ${#_abs[@]} )) || return 1
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#_b[@]}; i++ )); do
        b="${_b[$i]}"
        [[ "$b" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40,64}$ ]] || return 1
        info+="100644 $b"$'\t'"${_rel[$i]}"$'\n'
    done
    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" GIT_DIR="$gd" git update-index --index-info 2>/dev/null <<< "${info%$'\n'}"
}

zb_test_issue() {
    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
    local f="$dir/.zb-test-issue-seq"
    local n=0
    [[ -r "$f" ]] && n="$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null || printf '0')"
    [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || n=0
    n=$(( n + 1 ))
    printf '%d' "$n" > "$f" 2>/dev/null || true
    local id
    id="$(printf '9%03d%04d' "$(( $$ % 1000 ))" "$n")"
    # Record it, so teardown removes exactly the refs THIS file minted rather
    # than every reserved ref it happens to find.
    printf '%s\n' "$id" >> "$dir/.zb-test-issue-minted" 2>/dev/null || true
    printf '%s' "$id"
}

# Goal fixtures get the same treatment: the marker makes zbuild/state/goal-<hash>
# traceable back to a test even though the hash itself is opaque.
#
# The hash is RECORDED as it is handed out, exactly as zb_test_issue records ids.
# Without that, goal refs had no teardown and no guard — which is precisely how
# the leak fixed in this branch survived a full identity sweep unnoticed. The
# derivation mirrors zbuild_goal_key: sha256 of the text with all whitespace
# stripped, truncated to 12 hex.
zb_test_goal() {
    local text; text="$(printf '[zb-test] %s' "${1:-fixture}")"
    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
    local h
    h="$(printf '%s' "$text" | tr -d '[:space:]' | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-12)"
    printf '%s\n' "$h" >> "$dir/.zb-test-goal-minted" 2>/dev/null || true

# ─── _artifact_persist_put_back <from> <to> (#1805, ADR-006 §3.6) ───────────
# Copy every file under <from> to the same place under <to>, skipping any file
# <to> already has (no-clobber). stage-io/ records are excluded (one run's
# model calls, not stage output). Identical semantics to _hydrate_put_back;
# extracted here so the runner's resume rehydration and the hydrate plugin
# share one implementation.
_artifact_persist_put_back() {
    local from="$1" to="$2" f rel
    mkdir -p "$to" || return 1
    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        rel="${f#"$from"/}"
        [[ "$rel" == stage-io/* || -e "$to/$rel" ]] && continue
        mkdir -p "$(dirname "$to/$rel")" && cp -p "$f" "$to/$rel" || return 1
    done < <(find "$from" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
    return 0
}

id: artifact-snapshot-coverage
name: Artifact snapshot coverage (#1878)
# Per-repo overlays must declare `extends:` (template-resolver requirement).
extends: simple
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

# A LEAF stage followed by a CYCLE, so one run exercises both snapshot call
# sites. Before #1878 the snapshot lived only on the leaf path, so `cycled`
# below — standing in for design / build / test, which is where most of a real
# run's output is produced — never persisted anything.
stages:
  - id: intake
    gate: auto
    roles: [intake]
  - id: cyc
    type: cycle
    stages: [cycled]
    until:
      stage: cycled
      field: verdict
      op: eq
      value: pass
    max_iterations: 1
    on_max: continue

stage_definitions:
  cycled:
    roles: [builder]

# same 24h gate get_resume_recommendation applies below — named once here so a
# caller that needs the question answered no longer has to re-derive it.
#
# Callers act on rc=1 in ways that are hard to reverse (reclaiming a dead run's
# worktree), so each is responsible for its OWN safety guard on the artifact it
# touches. This predicate answers "is a process still working here?", never
# "is destroying this safe?".
zbuild_run_is_live() {
    local state_file="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$state_file" && -f "$state_file" ]] || return 1

    local status updated_at
    status="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.status' '')"
    [[ "$status" == "in_progress" ]] || return 1

    updated_at="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.updated_at' '')"
    [[ -n "$updated_at" ]] || return 1

    local updated_epoch now_epoch age_seconds
    updated_epoch="$(_zbuild_iso8601_to_epoch "$updated_at")"
    now_epoch="$(date -u +%s)"
    age_seconds=$(( now_epoch - updated_epoch ))
    [[ $age_seconds -lt 86400 ]]
}

    updated_at="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.updated_at' '')"

So the cycle-orchestrator DOES read `_persisted_iter` unconditionally (no `_ZBUILD_PIPELINE_RESUME_MODE` guard). And `_ZBUILD_PIPELINE_RESUME_MODE` is NOT exported from runner.sh.

Now let me understand the actual regressions:

For a fresh cycle run:
- `_cycle_state_init` uses `//=` to initialize `cycle_iterations[$id]` with `current_iter: 0`
- `_persisted_iter = 0` (since it was just initialized to 0)
- `_start_iter = 1`
The cycle runs fresh from iteration 1. If it was interrupted at iteration 1, it resumes from iteration 2 and skips the one already done. For a nested loop, I'm checking how the inner cycle's state carries over when the outer loop runs it again.

I'm seeing that the inner cycle would restart at iteration 3 on the second outer pass, because `//=` keeps the old `current_iter=2`. The fix is to reset that counter when we aren't resuming, and to export `_ZBUILD_PIPELINE_RESUME_MODE` from runner.sh so the orchestrator can tell the difference.

I need to check whether the orchestrator's `_persisted_iter` guard is what SPEC-7 depends on, so I'm going to run the resume-loop-state test.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: all three resume entry paths invoke _runner_resume_rehydrate before
# the dispatch loop. (issue #1805, ADR-006 §3.5)
#
# SPEC-9 [code]: All three resume entry paths (--resume flag to runner.sh,
#   auto-resume on detecting status=interrupted, zbuild pipeline resume
#   --run-id) invoke _runner_resume_rehydrate before the dispatch loop.
#   Its test must FAIL on the code as it was before this change.
#
# Three sub-tests, each with a separate work repo, state dir, and events dir:
#   Path 1 — bash runner.sh --resume
#   Path 2 — bash runner.sh (no --resume; state status=interrupted → auto_resume)
#   Path 3 — bash zbuild pipeline resume --run-id
#
# Discriminating assertion for all paths: intake-result.json is present in
# ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR after the runner call (artifact restored from state branch).
# Before this change: no rehydration → artifact absent → FAILS.
# After this change: _runner_resume_rehydrate restores it → PASSES.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
ZBUILD_CLI="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/zbuild"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/state/artifact-persist.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/artifact-persist.sh"

print_test_header "resume-entry-points — all resume paths rehydrate artifacts (#1805)"
setup_test_env "resume-entry-points-1805"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

# Common mock plugins for all three paths.
mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
# cycled sub-stage used by the artifact-snapshot-coverage cyclic fixture (SPEC-13 sub-case).
mock_plugin_factory "cycled" "agent" 0 "" "builder" >/dev/null
PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"

# ── Shared helper: set up a work repo with a state branch for one path ──────────
# Usage: _setup_path_state <label> <issue_id> → sets:
#   P_WORK_REPO, P_STATE_DIR, P_STATE_FILE, P_EVENTS_DIR, P_EVENTS_JSONL
_setup_path_state() {
    local label="$1" issue_id="$2"

    P_WORK_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo "ep-${label}")"
    install_template_overlay "$P_WORK_REPO" runner-state-dir-minimal

    P_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-state"
    P_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-events"
    P_STATE_FILE="$P_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
    P_EVENTS_JSONL="$P_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
    mkdir -p "$P_STATE_DIR/artifacts" "$P_EVENTS_DIR"

    # Write the intake artifact so the snapshot captures it.
    printf '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"prior-run intake"}' \
        > "$P_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

    # Snapshot onto the state branch.
    local _snap_rc=0
    ( export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$P_STATE_DIR"
      cd "$P_WORK_REPO" && _artifact_persist_snapshot "$P_STATE_DIR" "$issue_id" ) \
        >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-snap.log" 2>&1 || _snap_rc=$?
    if [[ "$_snap_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
        assert_fail "setup-${label}: snapshot to state branch failed" \
            "rc=$_snap_rc; $(cat "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-snap.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -5)"
